chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Umari, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who comforts the bereaved, Allah will shade him in the Shade of His Throne on the Day when there is no shade except His.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.الثَّكْلَى: The bereaved (specifically referring to a woman who has lost a child or husband, often used generally for the grieving)
key_terms.يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ: The Day when there is no shade except His

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for comforting the bereaved in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain tracing back to Imam Ali (AS), establishing the act of consoling the bereaved as a highly meritorious deed with eschatological rewards. The promise of divine shade under the Throne specifically addresses the scarcity of shade on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing Allah's direct protection for those who alleviate the sorrow of others. This narration underscores the social and spiritual importance of empathy in Shia ethics, linking interpersonal kindness to ultimate divine mercy.
